items.title: The Golden Bull
items.text: Charles IV's Golden Bull, issued at Nuremberg and Metz, fixed who elected the king: seven prince-electors, three archbishops (Mainz, Cologne, Trier) and four secular princes (Bohemia, the Palatinate, Saxony, Brandenburg).

items.title: Luther's theses
items.text: Martin Luther, a monk and professor at Wittenberg in Electoral Saxony, published 95 theses against the sale of indulgences. Within a few decades many princes and most imperial cities had turned Protestant.

items.title: Diet of Worms
items.text: Before Emperor Charles V and the princes, Luther refused to recant. The Edict of Worms outlawed him, but his prince, Frederick the Wise of Saxony, hid him at the Wartburg.

items.title: Peace of Augsburg
items.text: Emperor and estates agreed that each prince chooses the faith of his land, Catholic or Lutheran: later summed up as 'cuius regio, eius religio'. Calvinists were not included.

items.title: Silesia goes to Prussia
items.text: In 1740 Frederick II of Prussia invaded Habsburg Silesia. The Treaty of Berlin (28 July 1742) ceded almost all of it to Prussia, which kept it after two more wars.
